name: llama.cpp on Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4): Bonsai-27B Q1_0 decode throughput, batch 1
unit: tok/s (tg64, mean of two interleaved runs: 61.97 and 61.34)
methodology: PER-REQUEST decode throughput at batch 1: -p 0 (no prompt) -n 64 -r 5 (five repetitions). Two interleaved readings taken on the same hardware and the same base commit: unpatched master 29.69 and 29.11 t/s; patched build 61.97 and 61.34 t/s. Mean 29.402 -> 61.657 t/s, i.e. +109.7%. The 61.66 stored here is the mean of the two patched readings. Hardware: 1x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm/TheRock 7.13. Correctness was separately verified exhaustively over all 65536 possible q values with bit-identical output to the reference, plus test-backend-ops MUL_MAT. OMITTED BY SOURCE: VRAM size, GPU clock, power limit, host CPU, driver version beyond 'ROCm/TheRock 7.13', KV-cache size, and thread count. The author explicitly notes no NVIDIA hardware was available, so the CUDA branch of the patch is unmeasured.
notes: Recorded for two reasons. First, it is the best-documented RDNA4 llama.cpp decode measurement I could find with a real command line, exact quantization, mean-of-repeats, and a baseline measured on the same machine in the same session - the methodology most people actually want from a community PR. Second, and more important for a knowledge base: it is a worked example of an AMD-SPECIFIC SILENT PENALTY. HIP has no hardware __byte_perm, so it lowers to a software routine, and the Q1_0 unpack was calling it 20 times per 32-element chunk, making Q1_0 decode VALU-bound on AMD rather than bandwidth-bound. Replacing it with one hardware v_perm_b32 per nibble doubled decode. The general lesson: sub-2-bp quantization formats can be pathologically slow on AMD through software lowering rather than through any hardware limit, so a llama.cpp tok/s figure on AMD is a statement about the build, not just the GPU. The PR's own caveat is preserved: Q1_0 still will not beat Q2_0 on this hardware even after the fix - that appears to be a property of sub-2-bp formats rather than of any implementation. ACCELERATOR ID CAVEAT: no accelerators/amd-radeon-ai-pro-r9700 record exists in this repo; planned id, validator will warn. measured_by is third_party and status draft because the PR author self-reports and discloses that an AI agent built the trees and ran the benchmarks - good-faith, not independently audited. DANGLING REF, LEFT UNRESOLVED (2026-10-04 cross-reference repair): format_id holds '2bit', a bit width rather than a record id. What was actually measured is llama.cpp Q1_0 on Bonsai-27B, a 2-bit trellis format; data/quantization/ has no Q1_0 record, and mapping it to gguf-iq1-s or to ternary would misstate what the number describes. Left unchanged. This record also already carries its own accelerator-id caveat in notes about a planned id.
